relationship: Unresolved identification of the remembered servant-word with the Davidic house promise
rationale: Psalm 118 does not name David, a house or offspring in its request to remember the word that caused hope. The fully read prayer in 2 Samuel explicitly concerns David’s house. Similar servant-and-word language supports no identification of that unnamed saying as this particular dynastic promise.

relationship: Unresolved classification of the lawbreakers’ idle tales
rationale: Psalm 118 calls the lawbreakers’ speech idle tales and says they do not keep the law. First Timothy rejects profane and old women’s myths. The contents of the tales are not given, so a shared identified class of stories or particular literary dependence is not established merely by disparaging narrative labels.

relationship: Unresolved relationship of completion and breadth to divine extremes
rationale: Psalm 118 contrasts an end seen to every completion with an exceedingly broad commandment. Zophar asks about finding a trace of the Lord or reaching the furthest things the Almighty made, then invokes height, depth, length and the sea’s breadth. The shared dimensional terms do not resolve what completion means or justify equating the commandment with Zophar’s unsearchable objects.
